points.quote: Its `dependencies` list the extension packages it wants. ... `theia build` (from `@theia/cli`) uses the generators in `dev-packages/application-manager/src/generator/`.
A Theia extension is an npm package, such as those under `packages/`. Its `package.json` has a `theiaExtensions` array ... Each entry names the compiled modules to load
`src/browser/` holds the frontend module, and `src/node/` holds the backend module. `src/common/` holds code and protocols shared by both. Electron adds `electron-browser/` and `electron-main/`.
Each of these modules is an InversifyJS `ContainerModule`. It binds services and contributions to the dependency injection container.
`src/browser/` holds the frontend module, and `src/node/` holds the backend module. `src/common/` holds code and protocols shared by both. Electron adds `electron-browser/` and `electron-main/`.
Its `package.json` has a `theia` section with the target (`browser` or `electron`) and its configuration.

The generators write `src-gen/`, which contains a frontend entry and a backend entry. ... The bundler generator also writes `esbuild.mjs` ... `theia start` (or `npm run start:browser`) runs the generated backend. ... serves the bundled frontend at localhost:3000. ... Electron works the same way, with a main process that hosts the backend.
